question: Should crawl-remote deployments adopt this permanent hidden D1 canary as a rollback-compatible production contract after the stacked query-provenance dependencies land?
rationale: Tests can validate workflow structure, but automation cannot decide whether durable hidden rows, predecessor-runtime support, future schema obligations, and the dependency landing order are acceptable production policy.

options.title: Approve with staged rollout proof
options.body: Accept the permanent canary contract after both dependencies land and require a redacted staged deploy-and-rollback transcript covering all six queries, fresh coverage, archive hiding, and exact release provenance.

options.title: Isolate the canary lifecycle
options.body: Revise the design to use a separately managed or explicitly migratable canary store so production archive schema evolution and rollback are less tightly coupled.

options.title: Pause the Gitcrawl deployment stack
options.body: Keep this draft and dependent PRs unlanded until maintainers choose a different production verification strategy.

recommendation.title: Approve with staged rollout proof
recommendation.body: Accept the permanent canary contract after both dependencies land and require a redacted staged deploy-and-rollback transcript covering all six queries, fresh coverage, archive hiding, and exact release provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the complete stacked Gitcrawl evidence and deployment implementation and is best positioned to provide the dependency and staged rollout evidence for the decision.
